title: New York to North Carolina Car Shipping | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: New York to North Carolina car shipping takes 1–3 days and costs $550–650 for a sedan. Routes and prices for Charlotte, Raleigh, Asheville and the bases.
h1: New York to North Carolina car shipping
heroSub: A short, cheap lane with same-week pickups. 500 to 650 miles down I-95 and I-85, 1 to 3 days in transit, and prices that benefit from sitting on the busiest corridor in the country.
intro:
New York to North Carolina car shipping is one of the better deals in auto transport. A running mid-size sedan on an open carrier typically costs $550 to $650 from the NYC metro to Charlotte or the Triangle, and the car is usually delivered within three days of pickup. North Carolina sits directly on the New York to Florida corridor, so every truck heading south wants to fill an open slot with a car it can drop along the way.

This guide covers the roads, the pricing, and how Charlotte, the Triangle, Asheville, the coast, and the military bases differ. Pickups run from all ten of our New York offices; Hempstead, the Bronx, and Westchester see the most North Carolina traffic. The quote tool beside this page gives you a live price.

sections.h2: Two roads south: I-95 to Richmond, then I-85 or I-95
sections.html:
Every carrier leaving New York for North Carolina starts the same way: the New Jersey Turnpike, the Baltimore and Washington beltways, then I-95 to Richmond. At Petersburg the route splits. Trucks for Durham, Raleigh, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, and Charlotte take I-85 southwest. Trucks for Rocky Mount, Fayetteville, and Wilmington stay on I-95.

A driver reaches the Triangle in one long day and Charlotte in a day and a half, so on-truck time is 1 to 3 days, with pickup usually 1 to 3 days from your first available date. From Albany or Buffalo, the carrier may come down I-81 instead, a shorter path to Asheville and Charlotte.

sections.h2: Why New York to North Carolina car shipping is a cheap lane
sections.html:
Auto transport pricing is mostly about how easily a truck fills up. A carrier running New York to Miami wants ten cars on board. If it leaves with eight, the empty spots cost the driver money for 1,300 miles. A car going to Raleigh or Charlotte fills one of those spots for the first 500 or 600 miles and frees it for another pickup in the Carolinas or Georgia. That partial-load math is why the lane prices well below what the distance suggests.

The New York to Florida flow also means capacity rarely dries up, even in the January snowbird peak. Enclosed is the exception: fewer enclosed carriers run the corridor, so it adds 30 to 50 percent and often a few more days of waiting. The car shipping cost page lists the SUV, inoperable, and holiday surcharges.

sections.h2: Charlotte, the Triangle, and the Triad
sections.html:
Charlotte is the largest destination on this lane. Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Truist all move people from the New York financial industry into Charlotte, often with a company-paid car move. Uptown and South End are high-rise and the truck will not get close; plan to meet at a lot near the I-77 or I-277 exits.

Raleigh, Durham, Cary, and Chapel Hill make up the Research Triangle, with tech and pharma plus Duke, UNC, and NC State. Campus deliveries work best at an off-campus apartment or a nearby shopping center. Greensboro, Winston-Salem, and High Point sit on I-85 and I-40 between the two, are served by the same trucks, and price the same with a slightly longer delivery window.

sections.h2: Asheville: smaller trucks and steep driveways
sections.html:
Asheville is the destination that most often needs a conversation before booking. The city is reachable on I-40 and I-26, but the houses that draw people there are up switchbacks in Black Mountain, Weaverville, Hendersonville, and the Pisgah foothills. A 10-car open hauler cannot make those turns or climb those grades loaded.

Two solutions. Meet the truck at a lot near I-240 and drive the last stretch, or book an enclosed carrier or a smaller 3- to 5-car hotshot rig that can handle mountain roads to the door. Expect Asheville to run $50 to $100 above Charlotte and take an extra day or two for pickup.

sections.h2: Wilmington, the Outer Banks, and why islands cost more
sections.html:
Wilmington is the end of I-40 and priced close to Raleigh. Summer is busy on the coast; book June and July deliveries at least two weeks ahead.

The Outer Banks are different. Nags Head, Kill Devil Hills, Duck, and Corolla sit on a long barrier island reached by the Wright Memorial Bridge, and Hatteras is further down a two-lane road. A hauler that goes out to Corolla comes back the same 50 miles with nothing to pick up. That dead-end mileage shows up as $100 to $200 over the Raleigh rate, a longer pickup window, and in the off-season sometimes no carrier willing to go. Many customers meet the truck in Elizabeth City or Kitty Hawk instead, which keeps the price near the standard rate.

sections.h2: New York to North Carolina car shipping for Fort Liberty and Camp Lejeune
sections.html:
Fort Liberty, still called Fort Bragg by most people stationed there, sits outside Fayetteville on I-95. Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River are near Jacksonville NC, about an hour east on US-17. Both get a steady flow of PCS moves from New York.

Trucks cannot deliver inside the gate, so the driver meets you just outside: the shopping centers on Bragg Boulevard in Fayetteville, or the lots along Western Boulevard in Jacksonville. Fayetteville is on the I-95 spine and prices like Raleigh; Jacksonville NC adds the US-17 detour and runs $50 to $75 more. Our military car shipping page explains orders-based scheduling and the active-duty rate.

sections.h2: Retirees, remote workers, and auction cars coming north
sections.html:
Retirees head for Pinehurst, Southern Pines, the Lake Norman towns, and Brunswick County. Remote workers land in Raleigh, Durham, and Asheville. Same-week pickup is realistic; a car booked Monday from Babylon is often in Cary by Friday.

The lane also moves cars north. The Charlotte area hosts major dealer and salvage auctions, and New York buyers ship their purchases up I-85 and I-95 regularly. Auction pickups need a paid invoice and gate pass before the carrier can load, and storage fees start after a few days, so book transport before the sale closes.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to ship a car from New York to North Carolina?
faqs.a: A running sedan on an open carrier is typically $550 to $650 to Raleigh, Charlotte, or the Triad. Asheville and the Outer Banks run $100 to $200 more because they are off the main truck corridor. SUVs add $100 to $250, inoperable cars add $100 to $200, and enclosed transport adds 30 to 50 percent.

faqs.q: How fast can you pick up in the NYC area for a North Carolina delivery?
faqs.a: Same-week pickup is realistic most of the year. Trucks leave the metro for the Carolinas and Florida daily, so a car booked early in the week is usually loaded within one to three days and delivered one to three days after that. Holiday weeks and the January southbound peak can stretch the window a day or two.

faqs.q: Can a car hauler deliver to a house in the mountains near Asheville?
faqs.a: Usually not to the door. Full-size haulers cannot manage steep grades, gravel switchbacks, or tight turnarounds with a load on. Most customers meet the truck at a lot near I-40 or I-26 and drive the last stretch. A smaller enclosed or hotshot rig can reach many mountain addresses for a higher price.

faqs.q: Does the truck go onto Fort Liberty or Camp Lejeune?
faqs.a: No. Carriers do not have base access, so the driver meets you just outside the gate, typically at a shopping center on Bragg Boulevard in Fayetteville or along Western Boulevard in Jacksonville NC. Give us your report date and we schedule the delivery to land before it. Active-duty orders qualify for a military rate.

faqs.q: What do I need to ship a car bought at a Charlotte auction to New York?
faqs.a: The auction needs a paid invoice, the lot or stock number, and a gate release before the carrier can load. Send us those documents with the booking so the driver is on the list. Most auctions charge daily storage after a short grace period, so book transport as soon as the sale closes. Transit north is 2 to 3 days.
